newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Zaire refugees flee across lake into Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: Zaire refugees flee across lake into Tanzania.

text.p: Thousands of refugees are crossing Lake Tanganyika into Tanzania as fighting between Zaire's army and rebels spreads along the lake's western bank, the U.N. refugee agency said on Friday.

The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) Tanzania office said 1,151 Zaireans had crossed into the Kigoma region on Thursday, bringing the total number of Zairean refugees there to 56,000 since fighting started in November.
"It's very, very difficult. For all practical purposes we're counting on more people coming across the lake," said Lennart Kotsalainen, deputy chief of the UNHCR's Tanzania mission.

Rebels fighting to topple Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko on Monday captured Kalemie, Zaire's main port on Lake Tanganyika, and say they are moving rapidly south through the mineral-rich Shaba region to the smaller port of Moba.
"We have serious problems with the Zairean refugees. We have a build-up again in the holding centres," Kotsalainen said.
Aid agencies are working to prepare a site for 50,000 Zaireans at Lugufu, 87 kms (55 miles) northeast of Kigoma, while 15,000 are stuck in overcrowded centres around the port town itself.

The problem created by the influx of Zairean refugees is compounded by the arrival of an estimated 500 Burundian refugees a day to join the 163,000 who have already fled a brutal ethnic war into the Kigoma region.
